summary: Frank Salomon held posts at the University of Iowa (~1978–1982) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1982–2014), where he taught Linda Jean LaMacchia.

Frank-Richard Hamm worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his doctorate at the University of Hamburg under Walther Schubring (1940–1948) and held posts at Hamburg (1958–1964) and the University of Bonn (1965–1973).

Franklin Edgerton worked in Indology, linguistics, and Buddhist studies, earning his Ph.D. at Johns Hopkins under Maurice Bloomfield. He was a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1913–1926) and Salisbury Professor at Yale University (1926–1953).

Franklin I. Gamwell worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Union Theological Seminary (~1960–1963) and served as dean of the Divinity School at the University of Chicago (~1980–1990).

Franz Aubrey Metcalf works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. He earned his Ph.D. from the University of Chicago (~1997) and served as an instructor at California State University, Los Angeles.

Franz Bernhard was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Waldschmidt and completed his habilitation at Goethe University Frankfurt (1965). He served as a professor at the University of Hamburg from 1966 to 1971.

Franz Bopp was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Antoine-Isaac Silvestre de Sacy in Paris. He held the Chair of Sanskrit at Humboldt University of Berlin (1821–1867) and was a member of the Prussian Academy of Sciences (1822–1867).
Franz Ferdinand Schwarz worked in Indology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Graz (~1953–1958) and later served as a professor there (~1976–1999).

Franz Heinrich Trithen was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Franz Bopp at Humboldt University of Berlin. He worked at the British Museum (~1844–1848) and was professor of modern languages at the University of Oxford (~1848–1854).

Franz Kielhorn studied Indology and linguistics under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as professor of oriental languages at Deccan College (1866–1881) and professor of Sanskrit at the University of Göttingen (~1881–1908).
Franz Xaver Erhard is a Tibetologist who earned an MA from the Free University of Berlin and Humboldt University of Berlin (~2004). He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn (~2005–2013).

Franz-Karl Ehrhard worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, completing his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen and habilitation at the University of Hamburg. He directed the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project (1988–1993) and was a professor at LMU Munich (2001–2012).
François Bizot is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. He held a post at the École française d'Extrême-Orient (~1966–2011).
François Chenet was a scholar in philosophy and Indology who studied at the École Normale Supérieure (1973). He both taught Hugo David and had David serve on his committee in 2012.
François Grimal is an Indologist who held positions at the École Pratique des Hautes Études and the École française d'Extrême-Orient.
François Gros was an Indologist who studied at the University of Lyon. He held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1977–2002), where he taught T. V. Gopal Iyer.
François Jacob studied at Lycée Carnot and the Paris Medical Faculty (~1938–1947). He held a post at the Collège de France (1964–1991), where he taught Matthieu Ricard.
Françoise Mallison is a scholar in Indology and religious studies who studied under Charlotte Vaudeville. She served as Directeur d'Études at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1989–2005).

Françoise Pommaret works in Tibetology and history/archaeology, having studied at INALCO and the University of Paris. She became a Directeur de recherche at CNRS in 2002 and held posts at INALCO and the College of Language and Culture Studies.
Françoise Robin is a Tibetologist who studied under Heather Stoddard (~1999–2003). She held a post at the Institut national des langues et civilisations orientales around 2004.
